P1.evidence: Setter notes read back cleanly and confirmed point by point - 'he brought me up to speed with your situation. So just to summarize, you're currently working as a truck driver, correct?... you're also big on biohacking... your carnivore.' No frame of any kind was set, no frame agreement, and no opening 'what are you looking for help with'.

P2.evidence: Work explored well - 'what does a typical morning look like for you on the road?' Injuries asked directly - 'do you have any injuries or any pains that are, like, from the past?' Training week and diet both covered in detail. Age, height and weight were never asked; the 240-to-180 history and the diabetes came out unprompted. Sleep and energy never touched despite a long-haul driving schedule.

P3.evidence: The only goals question was a why-now - 'what is it that made you decide right now, the specific point in time, to start looking into adding kettlebells more seriously?' The 10 pounds of muscle and the leg focus were volunteered. No deep-goal work at all: no bridge past the physical, no impact-on-others, no identity or legacy. The rep disqualified at 00:15:12 before any of it.

P4.evidence: Best-run phase on the call. 'What's actually happened when you try to figure it out on your own? Like, what's getting in the way?' produced the gap in the prospect's own words - 'just a really lack of knowledge and lack of technique.' Past attempts were only lightly covered and the why-didn't-it-stick and information-isn't-the-problem moves never ran.

P5.evidence: Rep disqualified the prospect from the coaching programme at 00:15:12, before any consequence frame could apply.

P6.evidence: No commitment check because the rep decided not to offer the programme.

P11.evidence: No close attempted on the coaching offer. The Primal University alternative was left to a follow-up email rather than transacted on the call.

objection_plays.detail: '$200 a month seems kind of expensive for just workout programs' and then a request for a first-month discount. No isolation, no SHOULD-I/HOW reframe, no financial picture. The rep screen-shared features in response to the first and simply said no to the second. Holding price was correct; running nothing was not.

Script gap in the opposite direction from the usual. The prospect tried to buy up - 'what if I had the money and still wanted to do it, you know, to get coaching to get like feedback on my technique so I can push myself more' - and the rep deflected him back down: 'first go do the primal university and then if you feel like after two three months that you're still stuck reach out to us again.' There is no play for a self-disqualified prospect who volunteers back into the offer, and a stated want was left unserved.

notes: Honest, fast disqualification and a clean price hold, but the discovery stopped at facts - the rep decided the fit from the prospect's routine at fifteen minutes without ever running a goals or consequence phase, so the judgement rests on no emotional evidence at all. When the prospect then asked to buy the coaching, there was nothing in hand to test whether that was real.
